description: Precast concrete New Jersey median barrier segment with the sloped lower face, vertical upper face and lifting-hook recesses on top.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Precast concrete road barrier segment in warm sandy buff-beige concrete, noticeably darker and warmer than a neutral mid-grey, with the characteristic profile of a wide base, a steeply sloped lower face stepping into a near-vertical upper face, two rectangular lifting recesses in the top face and flat butt ends Materials: Warm buff-beige weathered concrete with formwork seams, black tyre rubber smears and diesel soot along the lower slope, dark moss and water staining at the base.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.94. 272/4,000 triangles, 1/4 draw calls, 1/3 materials, 1/6 unique geometries, one 512 px canvas at 1.3 MB.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 2.036 x 0.80 x 0.60 m (12 mm key tongue included); section from the proxy half-depth profile scaled 0.60/0.66, band table mean |delta width| 0.024, |delta depth| 0.036 H with the residual in the foot bands (the DECLARED depth). The silhouette now carries what the plate's does and the first build's did not: three notches cut through the toe, a capping that overhangs the upper face by 14 mm and steps back at its own top edge, and a chamfer on the bottom arris, the lip break and the slope nose.
Two 0.13 x 0.062 holes cut through BOTH cap steps -- 0.045 m deep against the first build's 0.03 -- at x +-0.62, with dark floors 2 mm above the body top. Visible at 0, 90, 180, 270 and the hero.

Three 0.20 m drainage notches at x = -0.66, 0, +0.66, cut to y = 0.070 by extruding the toe in four spans instead of the whole length. They are gaps, not the dark plates 1 mm proud of the lip that the first build painted on: they break the silhouette at all four turntable azimuths and their cut ends and ceiling are real surfaces.

Measured against the plate over matched crops: upper face renders luma 139.4 sd 11.0 against 139.6 sd 12.3; lower slope 159.3 sd 19.1 against 157.3 sd 21.6; capping 178.3 sd 31.5 against 177.5 sd 35.0. The normalised row profile tracks the plate's over 12 bands within 0.08. The first build rendered the face at 146.7 with sd 5.9 -- right hue, half the spread. The spread is made of 900 air-bubble pinholes at ~1 mm, 11 swept tyre scuffs over the 0.13-0.44 height band, one form seam per 0.8 m and 44 cloud patches.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's chipped end corner is deliberately not modelled: the segment tiles end to end.
